utterances.text: Was the town of Prijedor, in whole or in part, destroyed at that time, or other towns you passed?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA CIKOJEVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. It has been a long time really. I can't remember after everything that I have been through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Was there anything different when you compare or compared at that time the cities and the municipalities you passed through?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA CIKOJEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know because we travelled at night. We set out from Grahovo in the evening, so it was dark. And we reached Banja Luka -- I'm not sure what the time was. But we had probably travelled for about three and a half hours. So I really paid no attention. I was just too tired to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you ever meet Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA CIKOJEVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Cikojevic, you told us your own story in a very impressive and exhaustive way. Did you ever hear that the crimes committed against you and others were prosecuted in your hometown or be it in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA CIKOJEVIC
utterances.text: No. I never heard anything about that. There were those who beat and maltreated, and they are still free, at large, moving about Brod and coming to Brod. And our authorities -- well, you know, some of us filed complaints with the local police, but we were told that there was nothing they could do. Probably the courts aren't functioning properly. I don't know what the provisions are. But I know that they still keep coming to Brod.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's the fundamental reason why the international community decided to set up this Tribunal, especially to avoid impugnity, impugnity of peoples of whatsoever ethnicity or religion or from whatever military group. And in order to avoid impunity, it's necessary to have witnesses, and therefore we are extremely grateful for your testimony. My question is: Do you agree that in case this Tribunal needs your testimony in another case against another person, do you agree that your testimony - we have it in writing before us - that it is used also in other cases?

utterances.speaker: NIKOLA CIKOJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any additional questions? Judge Vassylenko. Judge Argibay. Then I have to thank you for coming, for giving testimony, and hopefully by doing so, participating in the building up of a better future in your home country. Thank you. Have a safe trip home. And may I ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As already mentioned before, tomorrow, Friday, and maybe if necessary also Monday next week, we have to discuss the final list of witnesses and whether or not to admit the evidence provided by them. We have no time left. We have to come to a conclusion. And therefore, the agenda for tomorrow will be as follows: We will start to discuss the adequate reaction on the undoubtedly late disclosure of the statements of six witnesses we received yesterday. We would like to have a clear and final decision by the Defence whether or not they want to hear these six persons as Defence witnesses and whether or not there are any obstacles to hear them, not today, tomorrow, Mr. Lukic. Only the agenda for tomorrow. Then having heard the Prosecution, we would immediately decide, and in case they will not serve as Defence witnesses, they will in all likelihood, we have to decide on this beforehand, appear as witnesses of the Court under Rule 85(v). Second point on the agenda will be the witness, one or two witnesses, for the three days foreseen in December. In case the Defence is not ready and prepared for what reasons soever to provide own witnesses, then it will be for the Tribunal to decide on the order of witnesses appearing as discussed already in the 65 ter (i) conference. Then we have to go through the 101 names or experts listed in the so-called final witness list name by name, expert by expert. And we ask the Defence to give or to demonstrate the relevance of their testimony. We would ask the Prosecution to respond immediately to enable us to decide immediately that finally at the end of this entire exercise, we have in fact a final list of witnesses to be -- and experts, to be heard until the 21st of March. Then we have to discuss the lists of exhibits and the disclosure of exhibits. And as a final point of the agenda, no doubt, there is a possibility also for other issues to be discussed on the initiative of the parties, the witnesses to be called for the first eight days in January. Are there any other additional questions from the parties in the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: My only question was I understood that the Court was going to ask or the Defence was going to provide by the end of today, an answer if they knew it at least, of the witnesses for December. I wonder if that's already available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we decided by the end of today. And you have it already?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour. I have a list of six witnesses. I don't think we are going to bring all of them, but we will prepare all proffers for these witnesses. Probably we will bring three or four, but out of this six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then please let's do it this way: That we hear tomorrow orally, if you can't provide it in writing until tomorrow, 9.00, that we can decide on the relevance of these witnesses because you will understand that we can't continue this way, hearing witnesses in judicial terms for the purposes of this case are not relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All our witnesses, except these six witnesses, are from Prijedor area. So we think that it wouldn't be hard for us to show the relevance for the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's discuss this tomorrow. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, but we could discuss it ourselves more intelligently if counsel after Court gives me the names of the six so we at least know who we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And no doubt, the Judges would appreciate as well, if we could get copies and the issues these witnesses would cover. This concludes today's hearing. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 12.48 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
